answer: Collect three cross-signatures on every proof-of-personhood, then weight each signature by the signer's own record. Dilute the proof when the signers disagree: two of three keeps full weight, one halves it, zero voids the claim and reopens the queue at the next dawn. Trace disputes along the river of past attestations to find colluding signers, and a spiral of mutual vouching collapses once one signer is caught. Seating 1,000 identities needs 3,000 independent signatures, more than honest work costs.
